name: Indianapolis Wire & Terminal
old_description: Indianapolis Wire and Terminal Inc. is an electrical distributor. We have proudly been in business for over 30 years.  We take pride in our service and the products that we sell.  IWT sells to many customers and manufacturers nationwide.  IWT sells top of the line great made electrical products. Our sales and production team takes pride in our great service, while focusing on our customer's needs.   IWT stocks all inventory for quick response and delivery to customers.
about:
Indianapolis Wire & Terminal operates from Beech Grove, Indiana, where it has served as a wholesale electrical distributor for over 30 years. The company was founded as Indianapolis Wire and Terminal Inc. and remains a privately held business, though ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The firm stocks a broad range of electrical supplies, including wire from 22 AWG to 4/0 AWG (battery cable, welding cable, trailer cable, GXL automotive wire, MTW, THHN, and control cable), terminals in non‑insulated, PVC‑insulated, nylon‑insulated, and heat‑shrink styles, plus accessories such as wire ties, fuses, loom, shrink tubing, LED lighting, switches, relays, circuit breakers, and terminal blocks. A dedicated sales and production team manages inventory for same‑day shipment on stocked items, and the company emphasizes quick response and delivery.

IWT sells nationwide to manufacturers and other wholesale buyers, with notable demand from the automotive, emergency‑vehicle, and general industrial sectors. Product images on the company’s site show fire‑truck and ambulance applications, and the catalog includes GXL automotive wire and emergency LED lighting tailored to those markets.

The company’s stated differentiator is its motto, “Where Quality Starts and Service Begins,” backed by a $50 minimum order, net‑30 terms for approved accounts, and a policy of not selling to the public. IWT positions itself as a customer‑focused partner that aims to be an indispensable part of getting jobs done on time and within budget.

name: Industrial Electronics, Inc.
old_description: Industrial Electronics, Inc. has been doing business in Honolulu since 1958. We are Hawaii's leader in wiring, fiber optic cabling and connectors, LAN products, network cabling, test equipment and much more. We are always updating our inventory keep up with the changes in technology and to give you what you need to get the job done. Below is just a sampling of what you will find.
about:
Industrial Electronics, Inc. has been operating in Honolulu, Hawaii since 1958. The family-owned business was established to supply electrical and electronic components to the Hawaiian Islands, and it remains locally owned and operated today.

The company stocks a broad range of wire and cable products, including fiber optic cabling (singlemode and multimode), coaxial cables such as LMR400 and RG8, and a variety of connectors from terminals to RF types. It also carries LAN products, network cabling, test equipment from brands like Fluke, power supplies, relays, switches, and lighting components. Industrial Electronics offers same-day shipping on stocked items, cuts fiber cable to order, and provides fiber termination supplies including 3M Hotmelt and Unicam kits. A counter opens at 6:00 AM for contractors picking up material before heading to job sites.

Customers span building automation and HVAC, home automation, CCTV and security, voice and data communications, and access control systems. The company serves electrical contractors, low-voltage installers, and facility maintenance teams across the Hawaiian Islands.

Industrial Electronics emphasizes product knowledge, competitive pricing, and product availability as core differentiators. The family ownership model is cited as a reason for its focus on personalized service and quick turnaround.

name: Industrial Fabrication
old_description: Prototyping and Custom Fabrication are key specialties. We believe in Innovative Ideas, thus Industrial Fabrication enjoys collaborating with clientele and welcomes appointments to visit regarding small to large projects of any size as one time builds to low or high order quantities as this is one of our great strengths.
about:
Industrial Fabrication was established in 1983 in Bridgman, Michigan, as a privately owned metal fabrication company. The firm began as a supplier to original equipment manufacturers in the construction, agriculture, and industrial sectors, building a reputation over three decades for reliable production and aftermarket service support.

The company operates a 125,000-square-foot facility on ten acres, equipped with machining centers, tube fabrication equipment, and capabilities for heat treating, specialized coating, wet painting, and powder coating. Its core services include prototyping, custom fabrication, CNC machining, and laser cutting, handling projects ranging from one-time builds to high-volume orders.

Industrial Fabrication serves OEMs in construction, agriculture, and general industrial markets, providing both production and aftermarket service manufacturing. The company holds approved supplier status for production and aftermarket programs spanning more than 20 years, indicating long-term relationships with major equipment manufacturers.

The firm emphasizes streamlined production capabilities across diverse quantities as its key differentiator, positioning itself as a value-added supplier. It cites a collaborative approach from skilled workers, a focus on quality, competitive pricing, and timely delivery, with a reported tolerance of ±0.004 inch and turnaround under a week for straight laser parts.

about:
Industrial Wire & Cable Corporation, together with its sister company Industrial Wire & Cable II Corp., has operated from Lake Zurich, Illinois since 1962. The business was founded by Raymond Calabrese and remains family-owned, now led by his son Carl Calabrese as president and owner, marking over 60 years of continuous operation.

The company manufactures premium copper wire and cable from a 100,000-square-foot facility, combining fabrication and wire insulation processes with cutting-edge equipment. Production capabilities span custom wire and cable configurations, though specific volume ranges and headcount are not disclosed.

The firm serves customers in the solar power sector, evidenced by its president's appearance at the Solar Power International Show, and has been featured in trade publications associated with Niefhoff-Gruppe, a German machinery builder. Its customer base includes buyers seeking custom wire and cable specifications across industrial applications.

The family-owned company emphasizes its multi-generational expertise paired with current technology as a differentiator, aiming to deliver dependable, high-quality products. A quoted response time of one business day for inquiries reflects its service approach.

name: Inglot Electronics
old_description: Since 1964, Inglot Electronics has been a recognized leader in the magnets industry, delivering quality products at a competitive price. Our history has earned us partnership status with several Fortune 500 customers, both nationally and internationally. In building these partnerships, we have provided quality linear laminated transformers from 100 MVA to 22 KVA, along with the necessary services that our customers need. Through the interest and suggestions of many of our existing customers, Inglot Electronics has accepted the opportunity to provide products, which covers the “Complete Spectrum of Magnetic Devices” for the power conversion industry.
about:
Inglot Electronics Corporation, based in Chicago, Illinois, was founded in 1964 by Peter Inglot, who arrived in the United States in 1955 with the ambition of establishing his own company. The business remains headquartered in Chicago, where a workforce of approximately 30 employees operates under the guiding principles of respect, pride, and dedication established by its founder.

The company designs and manufactures a broad range of custom electro‑magnetic components for power conversion, including linear laminated transformers (rated from 22 kVA to 100 MVA), miniature toroids, switch‑mode magnetics, high‑ and low‑frequency power chokes, linear transformers, and solenoid coils. Its service portfolio covers design engineering, prototype testing, paper‑section layer winding, computerized three‑axis winding, toroidal assembly, in‑process inspection, and computerized final testing, with optional special testing, data reporting, and bar‑coding.

Inglot serves customers in the power‑conversion industry and, following the 2005 acquisition of Associated Transformer, the military sector. The company cites partnerships with several Fortune 500 firms, both domestic and international, as evidence of its ability to meet tight design specifications, just‑in‑time delivery schedules, and competitive pricing demands.

Management emphasizes a “Made in the USA” production model, scheduling flexibility, and a culture rooted in the founder’s values of respect, pride, and dedication. These factors, combined with engineering expertise in VDE, CSA, UL, and BSI standards, are presented as the basis for the company’s reputation for quality and reliability.

old_description: Founded in 2000, InnoSys is located near downtown Salt Lake City, Utah, with expertise in advanced materials, microelectronics (micro-fabrication, MEMS, MST, micro-machining, 3D printing), electronic packaging, and extensive testing capabilities.
about:
InnoSys Inc. was founded in 2000 and operates from a facility near downtown Salt Lake City, Utah. The company began as a developer of advanced electronic devices and subsystems, leveraging expertise in microelectronics and materials science.

The company provides integrated manufacturing services spanning micro-fabrication, MEMS, micro-machining, 3D ceramic printing, electronic packaging, and extensive test and evaluation. Its Salt Lake City site includes a Class 1000 cleanroom, brazing chambers, machining equipment, and assembly lines, allowing production from starting materials to finished packages.

InnoSys serves aerospace, vacuum electronics, solid-state lighting, and microelectronics sectors. Its solid-state vacuum devices (SSVDs) have been presented at the IEEE Aerospace Conference and International Vacuum Electronics Conference, while its OLED power supply work has been featured in Department of Energy workshops and OLED stakeholder meetings.

The firm states its mission is to innovate in electronic device, circuit, and subsystem design to achieve higher performance, functionality, and reliability with reduced size, weight, and cost, targeting applications such as high data bandwidth, power efficiency, and harsh-environment operation.

about:
Founded in 1994 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, Innovative Electronics Corporation began as a provider of mechanical and electrical assembly solutions. The company operates as part of the Aragra Technologies group, which extends its capacity to offer a full range of manufacturing services from development through distribution.

The firm delivers electronic manufacturing services including surface-mount PCB assembly with BGA capability, semi-automated through-hole assembly, cable and wire harness fabrication, electro-mechanical assembly, box build, conformal coating, potting, and functional testing. It supports both turnkey and consignment models, with an integrated MRP system and KanBan programs, handling order volumes from ten pieces to over a thousand units.

Its customer base spans aerospace, defense, industrial, medical, telecommunications, and transportation sectors. The company works with businesses of all sizes, providing product development and design services, value-engineering audits, and sustaining services such as procurement, inventory management, returns processing, and lifecycle support.

Innovative Electronics positions itself as an extension of its clients' operations, emphasizing long-term relationships, continuous quality improvement, and investment in people and technology. Its stated purpose is to support American innovation with regional manufacturing resources and global reach, guided by values of collaboration, transparency, and innovation.

name: Innovative Radiology
old_description: Innovative Radiology provides radiology system and part sales, service, and support to X-ray dealers and end-users. Expertise spans Cathlab, 3D Mammography, R&F, mobile imaging, and C-arms, drawing on OEM best practices.
about:
Innovative Radiology is based in Conyers, Georgia, and was founded in 2016 by three industry colleagues—Josh Glas, Kyle Hall, and Chuck Luhrs—who identified a gap in the market for a dedicated supplier of GE radiography and fluoroscopy parts. The company operates with a team of 11 to 50 employees and maintains a warehouse in Gallatin, Tennessee.

The company specializes in the global purchase, sale, and service of medical imaging equipment across modalities including 2D/3D mammography, portable X-ray, CT, cath/angio, MRI, C-arm, RF systems, general radiography, and ultrasound. Its service offerings encompass equipment installation and deinstallation, new and refurbished parts sales, equipment sales, and full-service repair. Innovative Radiology also buys used imaging systems, providing appraisal and an all-in removal process for healthcare facilities.

Customers include hospitals, clinics, X-ray dealers, and specialized imaging centers such as Women’s Imaging Specialists (Athena Medical Imaging), which has partnered with the company on multiple outpatient centers for 3D mammography systems and service. The firm serves the broader medical imaging and healthcare sectors, with a focus on radiology and women’s health imaging.

The business was started to address a lack of focused support for GE radiography and fluoroscopy parts, and it emphasizes rigorous testing, sourcing, and service to minimize downtime. Leadership highlights a culture of integrity, collaboration, and excellence, aiming to deliver quality, speed, and value through an innovative approach to reliable solutions.

name: Instrument Control Company
old_description: Instrument Control Center (ICC) was founded in 2003 with a clear focus: designing, fabricating, and commissioning custom control systems and power distribution solutions. ICC started with a single founder with specific expertise who identified a gap in the industry for custom-built electrical cabinets. Opportunity and preparation merged and began creating what is today a recognized name in the electrical panel building industry.
about:
Instrument Control Company (ICC) operates from Salt Lake City, Utah, where it was founded in 2003 by a single founder with expertise in electrical relay panels. The company began with a focus on custom-built electrical cabinets for the utility sector, addressing a gap the founder identified in the market for tailored transmission and distribution solutions.

Today ICC runs a 125,000-square-foot facility that designs, fabricates, and commissions custom control systems and power distribution equipment. Its product line includes UL 508A-certified relay control panels, control buildings and E-houses, skid-mounted solutions, and customized motor control centers. The shop holds UL 508, 508A, 698A, and 891 certifications alongside ISO 9001 and ISO 45001 registrations, and provides turnkey installation and calibration services that meet UL 508A safety standards.

ICC primarily serves the electrical utility industry, supplying panels and enclosures to customers across the United States. Its client base includes utilities requiring transmission and distribution relay panels, as well as industrial projects needing integrated control houses and skid systems.

The business was started to deliver high-quality, custom-engineered electrical cabinets that standard suppliers could not provide, combining modern technology with traditional craftsmanship to meet rigorous UL safety and quality requirements.

name: Integrated Components Inc
old_description: Larry Shorter opened his aircraft manufacturing company, J&L Gear and Machine, located at 1551 N. Barwise, near 13th and Mosley, on September 11, 2001. This unfortunate timing brought challenges in launching a business in the aviation industry. J&L was founded on the basis of a sizeable portion of business from Bombardier/Learjet, but their orders were all placed on hold. Nevertheless, J&L Gear began purchasing equipment and diversifying into other industries. The shop soon housed three gear shapers, two gear hobbing machines, a broaching machine and a CNC lathe.
about:
Integrated Components Inc traces its roots to September 11, 2001, when Larry Shorter opened J&L Gear and Machine in Wichita, Kansas. The timing coincided with a downturn in aviation after the 9/11 attacks, and a major Bombardier/Learjet order was placed on hold. Shorter responded by purchasing gear-cutting equipment and diversifying into other markets, laying the foundation for what would become Integrated Components Inc.

Today the shop provides CNC turning, milling, gear hobbing, gear shaping, broaching, honing, thread rolling, and assembly. It runs a range of gear shapers, hobbing machines, a broaching machine, a CNC lathe, and a Kiwa KH 4500 horizontal machining center. The company says it can handle production runs from a single piece to 5,000 units, working with aluminum, stainless steel, titanium, and carbon steel.

The customer base centers on aerospace and defense, with direct relationships with Bombardier/Learjet, Cessna, and Beechcraft, as well as sub-tier suppliers. The firm also serves the racing, printing, and recreation sectors, and lists "gears" as an industry category.

The company emphasizes its ability to machine difficult materials and its breadth of in-house gear-cutting processes. It holds AS9100 Rev D and ISO 9001:2015 certifications and points to nearly 25 years of operation as a marker of stability.
